UserProfile.title: UserProfile
UserProfile.description: Represents a user's profile within 'The Crochet Studio' application, storing essential contact and display information.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserProfile entity.

email.description: The user's email address, used for communication.

displayName.description: The user's display name or preferred name.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the user profile was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the user profile was last updated.

Product.title: Product
Product.description: Represents a handcrafted crochet product available for sale, showcased in the featured gallery.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Product entity.

name.description: The name of the crochet product.

description.description: A detailed description of the product, highlighting its features and craftsmanship.

mainImageUrl.description: The URL for the primary image of the product, used for display.

additionalImageUrls.description: An array of URLs for additional images of the product from different angles or close-ups.

category.description: The category the product belongs to (e.g., 'Blankets', 'Apparel', 'Home Decor').

materials.description: An array of materials used to create the product (e.g., 'cotton', 'wool', 'acrylic').

isFeatured.description: Indicates if the product should be displayed in the featured products gallery.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the product was added to the catalog.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the product information was last updated.

CustomOrder.title: CustomOrder
CustomOrder.description: Represents a customer's request for a bespoke crochet item.

id.description: Unique identifier for the CustomOrder entity.

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile who placed the custom order. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N CustomOrder)

title.description: A brief title for the custom order request (e.g., 'Custom Baby Blanket').

description.description: Detailed description of the customer's custom order request, including specifications and personalization details.

status.description: The current status of the custom order (e.g., 'Pending', 'Drafting', 'Approved', 'In Progress', 'Completed', 'Cancelled').

referenceCrochetIdeaId.description: Optional reference to a CrochetIdea entity if the custom order is based on a saved or AI-generated idea. (Relationship: CrochetIdea 1:N CustomOrder)

requestedCompletionDate.description: The customer's requested date for the order to be completed.

priceQuote.description: The quoted price for the custom order once details are finalized.

depositRequired.description: The amount of deposit required for the custom order.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the custom order request was submitted.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the custom order information was last updated.

CrochetIdea.title: CrochetIdea
CrochetIdea.description: Represents a conceptual crochet design, potentially generated by the AI tool or saved by a user.

id.description: Unique identifier for the CrochetIdea entity.

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile who generated or saved this idea. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N CrochetIdea)

title.description: A concise title for the crochet idea, either AI-generated or user-provided.

description.description: A detailed description of the crochet idea, including design elements and aesthetic concepts.

suggestedMaterials.description: An array of materials suggested for this crochet idea (e.g., 'merino wool', 'bamboo yarn').

suggestedColors.description: An array of colors suggested for this crochet idea (e.g., 'teal', 'cream', 'sage').

moodOrStyle.description: Describes the overall mood or style of the crochet idea (e.g., 'boho', 'minimalist', 'vintage').

inspirationImageUrl.description: An optional URL to an image providing visual inspiration for the idea, if available (AI-generated or user-uploaded).

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the crochet idea was created or saved.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the crochet idea was last updated.

params.name: customOrderId

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user who owns this crochet idea, matching 'request.auth.uid'.

params.description: The unique identifier for a specific crochet idea.

firestore.reasoning:
The recommended Firestore structure is designed to be secure, scalable, and debuggable, explicitly addressing the reported permissions error and adhering to all core design principles. The primary strategy revolves around **Authorization Independence via Denormalization** and **Structural Segregation** to simplify security rules.

To resolve the immediate 'Missing or insufficient permissions' error for listing `/products`, the `/products` collection is designated for public read access. This is a direct application of **Structural Segregation** (Principle B) where all documents in `/products` share the same security posture: publicly viewable. This enables **Query As Permission (QAPs)** as the entire collection can be listed without needing client-side filters or complex server-side rule logic, directly facilitating the 'Featured Products Gallery' UI requirement.

For user-specific and private data (User Profiles, Custom Orders, Crochet Ideas), a hierarchical path structure under `/users/{userId}/...` is consistently applied. This aligns with **Access Modeling Strategy C (Hierarchical Paths for User-Owned Data)**. Each document in subcollections like `/users/{userId}/customOrders` and `/users/{userId}/crochetIdeas` inherently carries its authorization context through the `{userId}` wildcard in the path. Crucially, each `CustomOrder` and `CrochetIdea` document also contains a `userId` field, matching `request.auth.uid`. This fulfills **Authorization Independence (Principle A)**: rules can check `request.auth.uid == userId` (from the path wildcard) without needing `get()` operations on a parent document to verify ownership. This also supports atomic operations for creating user-owned data.

Global roles for administrative access, if required (e.g., for managing products), would leverage a dedicated top-level collection like `/roles_admin/{uid}`. This follows **DBAC (Principle B)** and uses **Existence over Content (Strategy C)**, allowing rules to check `exists(/databases/$(database)/documents/roles_admin/$(request.auth.uid))` for authorization, avoiding complex lookups.

This structure ensures clear intent for data access: public collections are globally readable, and private collections are path-segregated and user-specific, making security rules straightforward and highly auditable. Denormalization of the `userId` into subcollection documents reinforces ownership checks, eliminating fragile `get()` dependencies.
